newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: German, Swiss take over CS Holding's Watt stake.
newsitem.headline: German, Swiss take over CS Holding's Watt stake.

text.p: A consortium comprising German energy companies Bayernwerk, Badenwerk and Energieversorgung Schwaben (EVS), Swiss utility Nordostschweizerische Kraftwerke (NOK) and Swiss financial group CS Holding will take over CS Holding's current stake in newly-formed Watt AG.

Earlier this month Elektrowatt, 44.9 percent owned by CS Holding, said it was spinning off its utility interests into Watt. At that time CS Holding said it was keeping its stake in both Watt and Elektrowatt.

A joint statement from the five companies said that after the consortium had taken over CS Holding's 44.9 percent stake in Watt, the consortium would make a public offer to the shareholders in Elektrowatt for their shareholdings in Watt.

"In the initial phase, the consortium is to take over the shares held by CS Holding at a price of 265 Swiss francs. These are subsequently to be offered to the public shareholders at the same price," the statement said, noting the price may be subject to a change following the due diligence review.

The Swiss partners will thus have a majority.
NOK also plans to offer part of its holding in Watt AG, which it took over Thursday, to other Swiss energy groups.
"This underlines the Swiss-oriented nature of the solution which has been found," the statement said.
The energy firms in the consortium also intend to step up their collaboration with Watt AG and its holdings.
